title: Best way for a beginner to get into serious film appreciation?

commenti.body:
I have a few ideas for you.

If it's available in your country, I'd highly recommend subscribing to the Criterion Channel. It's simply the world's best, most extensive library of classic films. Furthermore, the retrospectives (they put out several each month) do a great job of putting films into context.

>What do I need to read/study in order to appreciate and start enjoying the critically acclaimed movies that I haven't enjoyed: Taxi Driver, Five Easy Pieces, No Country for Old Men.

Well, different people are going to enjoy different things, and I'm not sure you can ever force yourself to like anything. That said, learning more about film could certainly help you appreciate the craft involved in these films and/or their importance in film history.

A few recommended books about film aesthetics and film history:

*Film as Art* by Rudolf Arnheim

*The Star Machine* by Jeanine Basinger 

*On the History of Film Style* by David Bordwell

*Farber on Film* by Manny Farber 

*Film as Film* by V.F. Perkins

*The Genius of the System: Hollywood Filmmaking* in the Studio Era by Thomas Schatz

*A Biographical Dictionary of Film* by David Thomson

I would second what my friend here suggests, but also...

Don't rush it. The best appreciation of film comes from just watching films and thinking about them. Chatting about them here if you like. 

Sometimes you'll watch a film and dislike it but come back to it 30 years later and you wonder why you didn't love it to begin with.  Or vice versa.

So I'd say, don't worry about what you've tried and didn't like, follow up with what you did like, find out what's like that, but moreso. 

From the list you've mentioned of what you enjoy I'd suggest Under the Silver Lake, Chinatown, and Taste of Evil (for noir type movies) and if you're feeling more exotic on that front you could try Mulholland Drive. 

Then from the Unforgiven pile I'd try The Assassination of Jesse James, Old Henry and The Wild Bunch. 

From the Cabinet of Dr Caligari pile, oh boy, there's a lot that could come from that, as it's the ancestor of a lot of imaginative stuff.  Nosferatu 1979 is one that comes from original Nosferatu. 

But as I said, the important thing is not to try to make yourself an expert cinephile but to ease into it like a warm bath.

Many thanks, I can get the Criterion Channel, although I do get Criterion Collection discs in the post so wondering if the streaming service has more content than the postal service.

I will check out these books, hopefully help me enjoy or at least appreciate the work of Fellini which I tried really hard to like.
Get the streaming service, it has a significantly broader catalogue of films.
